- `governance_rules/OD-01` — "The pickable board's stored order is produced by exactly six ranking keys applied in this sequence: `automation_rank` nulls last, then tier (`now` before `next` before everything else), then the numeric part of `priority_class` ascending, then the M5-02 filing lane"
- `governance_rules/OD-43` — "`pz-rank-intent` instructs the Prioritizer to order tickets by project milestone order, then `supports_class` (P1 first, none last), then `priority_class`, then the filing lane, then `predicted_cycles`, then queue — an order that does NOT agree with the one the picker actually uses"
- `skill_profiles/pz-rank-intent/method` — "Order them: (1) project milestone order when the set spans milestones of one project; (2) supports_class, P1 first, none last; (3) priority_class, P1 first; (4) filing lane (filed before 2026-08-21 first); (5) predicted_cycles, cheapest first, unknown last; (6) queue."

**Proposed resolution:** OD-01 (public.recompute_backlog_queue()) is the executing home; the census already marked OD-43 'amend — NAMED CONTRADICTION'. Either the rank Intent adopts the picker's key order or OD-01 gains supports_class as a key — a John decision, then one Skill-row edit under a directive (gated).

**Ruling:** scripts/rank-backlog.js writes the Prioritizer's result as backlog_items.automation_rank, and recompute_backlog_queue() applies automation_rank as its leading key (OD-01). So pz-rank-intent's order (milestone, supports_class, class, lane, predicted_cycles, queue) decides the ranked head of the board, and OD-01's remaining keys order everything below it. They are layered, not contradictory. But OD-43 calls it a NAMED CONTRADICTION, runner-cycle.md:2487 says automation_rank sits 'above all six' keys with a 1-6 domain (the live values are -35 and -34), and M5 req :465 calls predicted_cycles the last term even though filed_at/id tiebreaks follow it. Separately, recompute_backlog_queue() coalesces filed_at to created_at, which M5-02 forbids. Today 0 of 559 open rows have a NULL filed_at, so this is latent. / No change to pick behaviour and no change to pz-rank-intent's method; it keeps John's supports_class order for the ranked head. Amend OD-43 from 'contradiction' to a statement of the two layers (the Intent produces automation_rank, which is OD-01 key 1). Reword runner-cycle.md:2487 to 'the leading of OD-01's keys; an open-ended integer, lower first, NULL = not ranked'. Amend M5 req :465 to 'the last ranking key before the filed_at/id tiebreaks'. Drop the coalesce(filed_at, created_at) in recompute_backlog_queue() so a NULL filed_at falls to the review bucket as M5-02 says, and add a tripwire that fails when an open row has a NULL filed_at. Close fingerprint 4637961d with this ticket. / CLOSED by AGT-89 (v7.0.567, cycle 280fdda4): migration agt89_filing_lane_filed_at_only dropped both coalesce(filed_at, created_at) terms from recompute_backlog_queue(); OD-01 and OD-43 rewritten as two layers in all three homes; runner-cycle.md now reads "the leading of OD-01's six order clauses" with the open-ended integer domain (live min -45, max 23 over 177 ranked rows); M5 req :465 now reads "the last ranking key before the filed_at date and the backlog_id/id tiebreaks"; ses-281 carries a tripwire that goes red on any open row with a NULL filed_at. pz-rank-intent.method was NOT edited -- that residue is fingerprint 6b42d2e1c8dad155, filed separately as needs-john. (devmanager, 2026-09-23)

- `governance_rules/OD-06` — "The standing drain picks its next member by filing lane first, then queue number, then `predicted_cycles` nulls last, and by nothing else; canonical: `public.drain_epic_next()`, the pick predicate's `ORDER BY`."

So pz-rank-intent's order (milestone, supports_class, class, lane, predicted_cycles, queue) decides the ranked head of the board, and OD-01's remaining keys order everything below it. They are layered, not contradictory. Reword runner-cycle.md:2487 to 'the leading of OD-01's keys; an open-ended integer, lower first, NULL = not ranked'. Amend M5 req :465 to 'the last ranking key before the filed_at/id tiebreaks'. - `governance_rules/OD-01` — "The pickable board's stored order is produced by exactly six ranking keys applied in this sequence: `automation_rank` nulls last, then tier (`now` before `next` before everything else), then the numeric part of `priority_class` ascending, then the M5-02 filing lane (`coalesce(filed_at, created_at)` before 2026-08-21 first), then `predicted_cycles` ascending nulls last, then `coalesce(filed_at, created_at)` ascending, with `backlog_id` and `id` as final tiebreaks; canonical: `public.recompute_backlog_queue()`."

**Proposed resolution:** OD-01 wins: its canonical is public.recompute_backlog_queue(), which orders filed_at, backlog_id and id after predicted_cycles. Amend the M5-07 register line at docs/RUNNER-GOV-M5-REQUIREMENTS.md:465 to read 'the last ranking key before the filed_at date and id tiebreaks'.

**Ruling:** scripts/rank-backlog.js writes the Prioritizer's result as backlog_items.automation_rank, and recompute_backlog_queue() applies automation_rank as its leading key (OD-01). So pz-rank-intent's order (milestone, supports_class, class, lane, predicted_cycles, queue) decides the ranked head of the board, and OD-01's remaining keys order everything below it. They are layered, not contradictory. But OD-43 calls it a NAMED CONTRADICTION, runner-cycle.md:2487 says automation_rank sits 'above all six' keys with a 1-6 domain (the live values are -35 and -34), and M5 req :465 calls predicted_cycles the last term even though filed_at/id tiebreaks follow it. Separately, recompute_backlog_queue() coalesces filed_at to created_at, which M5-02 forbids. Today 0 of 559 open rows have a NULL filed_at, so this is latent. / No change to pick behaviour and no change to pz-rank-intent's method; it keeps John's supports_class order for the ranked head. Amend OD-43 from 'contradiction' to a statement of the two layers (the Intent produces automation_rank, which is OD-01 key 1). Reword runner-cycle.md:2487 to 'the leading of OD-01's keys; an open-ended integer, lower first, NULL = not ranked'. Amend M5 req :465 to 'the last ranking key before the filed_at/id tiebreaks'. Drop the coalesce(filed_at, created_at) in recompute_backlog_queue() so a NULL filed_at falls to the review bucket as M5-02 says, and add a tripwire that fails when an open row has a NULL filed_at. Close fingerprint 4637961d with this ticket. (devmanager, 2026-09-23)
